model_output.verdict: A store manager with strong results in Charlotte and a two-store turnaround claim that needs backing.
write_up: Your resume shows a progression from department supervisor to store manager at Carolina Home & Garden. The Charlotte role makes a strong case: a recruiter can see the store you run and the changes in sales, turnover and shrink.

The turnover line is a great model because it connects fixed schedules to a drop from 68% to 41%. The headline promises two store turnarounds, though the Gastonia roles don't yet show what changed there.
Start with that headline. Add what you did and what changed at each store, if you can, or narrow the claim to the turnaround your resume shows.

cards.line: Retail store manager who has turned around two underperforming stores in a 60-store regional chain.
cards.cannot_tell: The Charlotte results are clear, but a recruiter can't see the second turnaround in the Gastonia roles. That makes the headline a bigger claim than the jobs currently back up.
cards.example: Retail store manager who has turned around two underperforming stores in a 60-store regional chain by [actions at each store], with [results at each store].
cards.question: What did you do at each store, and what changed?

cards.line: - Cut annual staff turnover from 68% to 41% by moving to fixed weekly schedules
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives a before and after and names the management decision behind the change.

fit.note: Your experience points most directly to store management. The Charlotte role shows responsibility for a $9.4M store and 42 employees, with several measurable improvements.
